decisions.reason: The proposed annulus counterexample is already compressible: push the boundary disk inward and its rim along the proper surface collar to obtain an interior disk with essential boundary. A compression disk is proper in the cut side, not necessarily in M. The geometric disk convention does not create the claimed false compression.

The Statement explicitly specifies the PL category, and F1 explicitly interprets irreducibility in that category. Thus the ball in 1.1 is PL by hypothesis, not by an unproved TOP-to-PL upgrade. Its contained cutting tori compress by F2, so the ball misses all cutting tori and lifts to the original cut component.

F5 originally asserted boundary-relative general position and extension beyond its quoted interfaces, leaving the disk moves unjustified as cited. The proof now doubles the neat comparison surface, truncates separated collars when boundaries coincide, and uses the existing q-times-velocity extension from the neatification supplier Proof 5.2 to fix the ambient boundary. Classification, disk isotopy, TOP torus conclusion, and full AC are preserved.

F2 inaccurately attributes rectangle product parameters to normal position. The proof already invokes F5, whose cited Proof 1.1 constructs every face-cell disk and extends its rectangular boundary map over the disk; Proof 4.1 supplies the inward collar. F2 now states only its actual marked cut-ball conclusion and attributes the rectangle construction to F5. The face count, interval-bundle hypotheses and mod-two inequality remain valid.

The title abbreviates the precise qualified Statement; it does not remove its hypotheses. The proof treats the TOP two-sided torus using its product collar, separates the ball into compact TOP sides, finds a noninjective boundary group by amalgam normal form, and transports a finite PL Loop disk through a fresh cut-side triangulation. No compatibility of the original torus with the ball triangulation is claimed.

Step 4.1 already invokes the coherent-normal-side argument. Orient a regular fiber near the exceptional core: all q crossings of any one horizontal meridian disk have the same coorientation sign. A returning disk approaches the same normal side of F at both ends, requiring opposite crossing signs; its endpoints therefore cannot belong to that same disk. With no intervening crossings the projected core interval lies strictly between adjacent distinct core points and is shorter than one core period. Radial ruling is injective even at the core, giving the claimed bigon between distinct disks and cancelling two intersections. The subsequent normalization, Euler count and cut interval-bundle argument retain their hypotheses. Read Hatcher Proposition 1.11 and the complete following horizontal-surface discussion, printed pp.16–18; the sign check here was carried out directly.

F2 falsely attributed a base surface and regular-fiber slope definition to its supplier. It now accurately cites the fiber models and explicitly supplies the boundary-circle-bundle slope convention. Applying annulus verticalization to each fibration preserves the original boundary-circle isotopy class; the two excluded orientable exceptions prevent any fibration replacement. The annulus-family coverage and the Statement are unchanged.
